activity.notes: Honda Tadakatsu (本多忠勝, 1548–1610), a military retainer of Tokugawa Ieyasu and one of the four leading Tokugawa generals, participated on the Tokugawa-led eastern side in the 1600 Sekigahara campaign. The historical reference entries distinguish his role as a military supervisor alongside Ii Naomasa and his contribution at Gifu/Sekigahara from any sovereign rulership. This is a sourced 1600 representative military-activity point, not a fictitious full career interval or a 1600 Tokugawa-shogunate office: the Tokugawa shogunate was established only in 1603. ATLAS reuses the existing Japan polity used for Tokugawa-era Person Activity; neither the clan nor the as-yet-unfounded shogunate is created as a new political state. Tadakatsu subsequently became lord of Kuwana in 1601; the later daimyo office is not backdated to the 1600 event.

sources.title: 本多忠勝 — 国史大辞典 (JapanKnowledge)
sources.citation_text: The historical encyclopedia identifies Honda Tadakatsu's 1600 Sekigahara role alongside Ii Naomasa in oversight of eastern-army commanders, and his death in 1610. It separately describes his career as a Tokugawa retainer.

sources.title: 本多忠勝筆書状 — 慶應義塾ミュージアム・コモンズ / Keio Object Hub
sources.citation_text: Keio's collection record identifies the surviving letter by Honda Tadakatsu (1548–1610), establishing the historical individual and his administrative direction to household officers.

sources.title: 関ヶ原の戦い — 国立公文書館 (National Archives of Japan)
sources.citation_text: Japan's National Archives dates the Sekigahara campaign to 1600 and distinguishes the Toyotomi-era coalition from the subsequent 1603 shogunate, so it should not be retroactively labeled Tokugawa Shogunate in 1600.

spatial_disposition.evidence: The historical campaign was at Sekigahara (present-day Gifu Prefecture, Japan), but this Person registration supplies no invented person-owned location coordinates or new polity geometry; reuse the existing Japan political identity and its independent spatial record.
